method: AST parsed every src/lib .ex file without project compilation; reviewed every listed function span below, and surrounding context for decision/usage/control helpers. Exact-body enumeration is complete for the stated syntax/threshold, but semantic review, near-duplicate coverage and the name sweep remain incomplete. No raw review unit promoted.

reviewed_clusters.assessment: Optional named/unnamed GenServer startup wrapper. __MODULE__ resolves differently at each site; matching text does not mean the modules should merge. No new generic process package justified by these six-line wrappers.

Equivalent-looking optional-name startup idiom, but four physical lines: excluded from the final >=5-line candidate population. Keep separate from the case form until nil/false semantics and callers are checked.
Always passes name option and differs from wrappers omitting name on nil. Four physical lines, outside final candidate threshold. Defaults also differ across heads. Do not merge by body hash alone.

Seven trim-empty-to-nil clauses in six modules. Common string primitive, but credential, account, decision and usage policies differ outside this clause. Read sibling clauses/callers before selecting a utility owner; preserve secret-specific handling.

Both usage query layers count missing attribution dimensions with the same reducer. A usage-owned helper may prevent drift; verify bump and input-dimension semantics and existing findings before promoting.

Six binary ISO8601-to-DateTime-or-nil clauses in five modules. This only covers their binary clause, not full parser policies or nonbinary inputs. Compare typed/date/invalid fallbacks before collapsing adapters.

Two recursive rotation implementations with the same rename/error-swallowing policy. Review append ownership, retention settings, tests and failure reporting before extracting a filesystem primitive; no rotation failure reproduced here.

Six control-character predicates match, five in the decision family and one in recent merges. Consolidate policy within the decision boundary first; cross-domain reuse needs explicit agreement on allowed whitespace and redaction ordering.

Three identical persisted timestamp readers preserve invalid_timestamp versus missing_or_invalid reasons. A decision persistence codec is a plausible owner; keep event/revision-specific validation and error envelopes.

Three orchestrator helpers share a 5000ms call and timeout/unavailable classification. Compare the separately matched timeout-parameterized helper before extracting; preserve each public operation timeout and failure contract.

Four usage storage records compute deterministic Erlang-term SHA-256 after dropping the string checksum key. A common codec is plausible, but persisted byte compatibility is an invariant: moving a function must not silently change the hash format.

Four AIUR_DEBUG readers agree on trim/lowercase and 1/true/yes. A single owner may be appropriate, but search the remaining variants and boot-time versus runtime reads before declaring the full policy population.

Two additional orchestrator helpers have the same timeout-parameterized call/error classification. They are a near-duplicate of the fixed-5000ms three-site cluster, not in that exact-body group. Preserve caller-supplied timeout semantics.

Both history servers schedule again on success and unavailable, broadcast sample count only on success, and bound retained samples. Inspected both take_sample/schedule/broadcast implementations: cache uses CacheInspector.history_sample; quota uses QuotaUsage.sample over a separately protected injectable snapshot. A small history-ring policy could be shared if more consumers justify it; identical callback text alone does not justify merging process identity, topics or data sources.

Both mark membership unavailable after attempting the terminal-pending marker, then swallow failures. Read both marker helpers: CommentWake pattern-matches identity in clauses; RetryEngine checks match? and joinable? in one function. Preserve joinability checks, call order and failure receipts in any membership-owned extraction. Do not replace these with a generic safe-call wrapper without those policy contracts.

Read both complete modules. Status attributes and route-resolution branches agree, but AnalyticsScope produces bare ticket-number telemetry keys while UsageScope produces repository-qualified Scope values. Share selected-member/health resolution within BuildOrder presentation; retain explicit telemetry and usage adapters and their different cache-key types. Matching decide bodies are not evidence that whole scopes are interchangeable.

Both tracker adapters dispatch optional expected_state with the same validation. The actual update and conditional mutation remain backend-specific; this small wrapper expresses their common callback contract. Prefer a shared conformance test before introducing a generic adapter delegation layer. Conditional-update atomicity is outside the evidence from this body match.

Verified Style and Text aliases resolve to the same renderer modules. Table separator ignores layout and reproduces Chrome.separator_row for the same width. Reuse a renderer-owned separator primitive or existing Chrome function; retain the table-facing arity if callers require it. No new cross-package formatting utility is needed; preserve ANSI-aware padding and narrow-width behavior.

Verified both Lifecycle aliases resolve to Aiur.BuildOrder.Lifecycle and both empty-list clauses return nil. Both hash sorted valid state/state_reason pairs, preserving duplicates; CatalogStore explicitly documents parity with Normalizer. Own this change signal in the BuildOrder lifecycle/metrics boundary instead of maintaining two implementations. Preserve nil for unresolved data, ordering invariance and duplicate multiplicity; this is an invalidation signal, not a collision-free identity.

Both wrappers normalize callback :ok versus all other results and rescue/catch failures to :error. CommentWake applies identity eligibility in its caller, while IssueSync invokes directly at this helper boundary. A membership-owned callback primitive can share this narrow operation; do not silently add or remove eligibility checks when combining callers. Related to the unavailable-marker cluster, not an independent package proposal.

Four six-line helpers read positive integer options with caller-provided fallback. This is a genuine small policy repetition but spans decision metrics, polling, recent merges and webhook delivery. A generic options package would add coupling for a trivial expression; retain locally unless a cohesive existing config boundary takes ownership. Each caller still owns which defaults and limits are valid.

Read neighboring clauses: decision API/query accept integers and strings and return nil otherwise; analytics additionally rounds floats; budget string parser is unguarded behind typed callers. String clauses use full-consumption Integer.parse identically. Do not replace entire functions with one permissive parser: float acceptance and invalid-input policy differ. Decision API/query are a stronger same-domain normalization candidate than a repository-wide number utility.

Read both complete fmt_elapsed clause groups: nonpositive values produce 0m; positive milliseconds round to seconds then truncate to minutes and emit h/m text identically. Candidate for a web-presentation duration formatter with explicit precision, preserving both negative/zero and hour-boundary behavior. This establishes matching source behavior, not runtime traffic or savings.

Both parse functions and their complete origin-detection callers match: git remote get-url origin, trim output, parse final two path segments, nil on command failure/exception. Reuse the existing Git origin boundary from init rather than maintain a second parser. Preserve current permissive SSH/HTTPS/path handling during extraction; this syntax does not validate the host or prove the remote is GitHub.

Both full clause groups agree on missing/type/length/control-character errors and invoke the same Aiur.SecretRedactor after validation. Shared decision-owned bounded text validation is cohesive; preserve trim-before-length, grapheme length, error field attribution, and redaction order. Relates to the previously assessed unsafe_control_chars cluster, not a second package proposal.

Both count distinct projected values only when all metadata records are successful, otherwise nil. Empty input yields zero; placeholder unassigned/unphased values count as groups. Source comments explicitly require catalog/graph parity. Consolidate with lifecycle digest in a provider-neutral BuildOrder metrics boundary, preserving unavailable versus zero and placeholder semantics.

Synchronous sample callbacks repeat the async history policy already assessed, but do not schedule the next timer. Both return :ok even when unavailable. Keep manual sample and periodic scheduling distinct in any ring-helper extraction; do not infer current source availability from the receipt. Related to cluster 244eea1e, not another process boundary.

Identical test-environment gates suppress default durable logging while production calls module-local resolve_default_path functions. Retain this safety behavior; matching wrappers do not mean process logs and GitHub request logs share destinations or retention. A shared persistence boundary must continue requiring explicit test paths and must not discover real user state in tests.

FileOps.regular_or_missing? and ProgressRetention.ensure_regular_file perform identical lstat preconditions. FileOps also has a DIFFERENT ensure_regular_file that requires an existing regular file and reports atomic_write_not_visible. This is a concrete naming trap: share regular-or-missing policy only, preserving post-write visibility checks separately. A precheck is not an atomic no-symlink guarantee; do not strengthen that claim without inspecting the actual write operation.

Three persisted-map readers return the same field-tagged missing_or_invalid error for absent/non-map values. Group with timestamp readers in a decision persistence codec, retaining per-record schema validation outside this shallow shape check. Accepting any map does not establish a valid nested record.

Reconciliation and webhook deposit accept positive integers plus positive fully parsed strings; CatalogStore has an unguarded string helper with binary dispatch at its issue_number caller. Matching string bodies support a narrow positive-number parser, not arbitrary identity equivalence. Preserve typed caller boundaries and repository-qualified identity outside the parser.

Both workers implement the same refresh-config then enabled? then scan skeleton under the existing PeriodicWorker behavior. Their refresh and scan implementations are module-local policies. Retain the explicit callback unless richer shared lifecycle evidence warrants abstraction; adding a second generic worker layer for this nine-line body is not justified.

Both remove only a path observed as regular, accept missing as success, reject symlinks/nonregular types and propagate filesystem errors. Candidate for a narrowly named filesystem operation shared by membership markers and ledger pending files. Preserve the error taxonomy and idempotent missing behavior; lstat followed by rm is not an atomic race-proof guarantee.

Full trim-to-nil clause groups match across Executor attention/CLI and provider request usage. Same implementation is real but these are separate semantic inputs. Executor-local reuse may be cohesive; avoid pulling provider accounting into a generic command utility. Related to earlier blank-string normalization cluster; not independent complexity savings.

All three full clause groups permit http/https URI with binary host, else nil. Call sites are rendered hrefs or presenter URL shaping. Centralize web outbound-link policy if consistency is required, without calling it host trust or SSRF protection: it performs neither a host allowlist nor a server fetch. Preserve renderer escaping and rel protections outside this parser.

Read BridgePort and BridgeSupervisor callers. Availability probing and actual Bandit binding parse the same host independently and both fall back to loopback on parse failure. Resolve address once in the bridge boundary so port probing and binding cannot drift. Preserve default-port scanning versus explicitly pinned port failure; changing malformed-host fallback would be a separate behavior decision.

Three BuildOrder option modules implement identical bounded-positive selection with caller-supplied key/default/maximum. A BuildOrder-owned options helper could share this pure policy while each service retains its limits, runtime-config cadence and defaults. Do not generalize all positive-option helpers: the previously assessed unbounded policy lacks this upper-bound contract.

Three source/sweep helpers accept repo_fun {:ok,{owner,repo}} binaries and lowercase both; other returned shapes become nil. They do not rescue callback exceptions, validate nonempty values, or resolve tracker-neutral identity. Share only within the GitHub repository boundary if extracted; preserve degraded listing and source-specific behavior in callers.

Three persisted string readers agree on nonempty binary and field-tagged missing_or_invalid; whitespace-only binaries remain accepted. Group with map/timestamp readers in the decision codec, preserving this shallow persisted shape contract separately from request-time trimming/redaction.

Both poll batches alias Aiur.TicketBranch and generate title-derived branch first, legacy second, deduplicating when equal. Put ordered branch candidates in the existing ticket-branch boundary so CI and comment lookup evolve together. Preserve known-branch precedence outside this helper; no API saving measured from consolidation.

Version/positive-integer persisted readers share the same positive-integer shape check and field-tagged error. Group with decision codec helpers, but retain record-specific supported-version validation; accepting a positive version number is not proving that version is supported.

Both resolve configured daemon log or the same LogFile default, then join a DIFFERENT @filename: telemetry.ndjson versus saturation.log. Share parent-directory resolution if owned by daemon logging; never coalesce the streams based on this body hash. Attribute values are part of behavior despite identical AST bodies.

Verified both aliases reference AiurWeb.FinancialDataAccess. Both require authorized capability state AND a typed verified context, else locked. Candidate for a single access-module gate used by both web runtimes; preserve the conjunction rather than accepting context alone or capability alone. This body review does not establish revocation coverage at every protected call site.

Read both normalize_key and accumulate_key implementations: atom/string keys normalize to strings; non-atom/string keys fail; collisions are rejected rather than silently overwritten. A decision-owned normalization helper can preserve this full contract. Do not replace with Map.new stringification, which would erase duplicate-field rejection.

Both AgentList safe_call wrappers collapse exceptions, exits and throws to nil. Candidate for local TUI reuse only after reviewing each caller purpose; do not promote broad failure swallowing into a repository utility. A nil result cannot distinguish unavailable from a legitimate nil return, and identical bodies do not justify extending that policy.

Both broadcast count best-effort but @topic and @message differ: github:cache:history/cache_history_sampled versus github:quota:history/quota_history_sampled. Related to the history-ring pattern already assessed. Preserve stream identity and failure policy; a shared helper needs explicit topic/message inputs, and this is not a duplicate notification stream.

Read bounded and reason decoders in both modules. Successful shape and uint64 maximum agree; reasons become a set using existing atoms. Failures differ intentionally: invalid_checkpoint versus invalid_block. Share coverage validation only with explicit error adaptation at each persisted-record boundary; equal top-level bodies currently call different error-producing helpers.

Verified ResourceStore, ModeRegistry and ViewStateSweep aliases resolve identically. Both issue sources subscribe to issue/labels/mode/recovery/divergence events in the same order. This is a coherent subscription-set candidate within GitHub source support; source snapshots, notifications and lifecycle remain distinct. Do not infer successful subscription from unconditional final :ok without inspecting returned errors.

Read both ticket_key helpers: both call TrackerIdentity.github_key, deduplicate valid keys and count rejected entries. Query has non-list fallback to empty while Scope helper lacks it. Share the list normalization primitive in usage identity/scoping, preserving each public entry point input policy; avoid counting duplicates as rejected tickets.

Both ensure a directory with the same agent-support error tuples, create a missing path with mkdir, and reject other lstat types including symlinks. Cohesive candidate for existing agent support installation ownership. Retain explicit unsafe/unavailable distinction and nonrecursive mkdir semantics; atomic script installation and credential handling remain separate review concerns.

Both best-effort unsubscribe bodies use different history @topic values. Related to the same history notification support pattern, not independently removable behavior. Preserve which process subscribes/unsubscribes and topic isolation in any extraction.

Both escape ampersand first, then angle brackets, double quote and apostrophe into identical HTML entities. Events sanitizer and web Markdown have different surrounding responsibilities; avoid making core events depend on a web module merely to reuse five replacements. Consider an existing low-level escape primitive only after checking exact entity output and double-escaping contracts; this does not make the entire sanitizers equivalent.

Best-effort subscribe bodies match but subscribe to separate cache/quota history topics. Group with broadcast/unsubscribe and sampling findings as one potential history-support abstraction, not five independent saving opportunities. Keep typed event ownership and unavailable behavior explicit.

Both require an existing regular file and attach the path to symlink/non-file errors, propagating enoent rather than accepting absence. Cohesive durable-log precondition candidate, but distinct from regular-or-missing helpers assessed earlier. Preserve error shapes and caller ownership of file creation; lstat alone is not an atomic filesystem guarantee.

Identical version-1 marker serialization and fsynced atomic write call different accepted reason domains: aggregate accepts any atom, ledger recovery only four corruption reasons. Share encoding/write mechanism with explicit reason validation at callers; do not widen ledger accepted inputs or lose sync_fun ordering. Callback exceptions are not normalized here.

Both GitHub pollers stringify targets, trim, reject blanks and preserve first occurrence through Enum.uniq. Candidate for poll-input normalization within GitHub events. This is neither positive-number validation nor repository identity checking; preserve supported String.Chars inputs and their failure behavior.

Read available? and same_run? helpers. Outcomes availability checks health healthy/partial only; RunSummary additionally requires run.valid?. Run-ID matching otherwise agrees. Thus identical reconcile bodies are NOT interchangeable predicates. A shared last-known-good policy must take explicit validity/availability rules or retain separate implementations; no defect or intended-policy equivalence inferred from the discrepancy.

Read both open_pull_request_head_ref helpers: same map lookup and head/ref extraction. Explicit branch map value takes precedence via || before nonempty-binary validation; an empty string is truthy and blocks fallback. Group known-branch resolution with guessed branches in polling support, preserving precedence during extraction; changing malformed/empty override handling is a separate behavior decision.

Same collision-rejecting reduce callback already inspected with normalize_keys. Preserve halt-on-duplicate after atom/string normalization; group into the decision normalization proposal, not a separately counted extraction or saving.

Both financial usage subscriptions map exceptions and exits to error unavailable while preserving normal return values. Candidate for shared FinancialData subscription adapter alongside the access gate. Do not collapse denial into authorization or omit per-connection verified context; throw handling is not present in this wrapper.

Both decision API and query reader catch exceptions/exits into store_unavailable, while retaining normal return values and not catching arbitrary throws. Cohesive decision-store adapter candidate, but review callers before changing error transport or broadening recovery. Do not generalize to nil-returning TUI safe_call wrappers.

Both aliases resolve to Aiur.GitHub.Client; both discard returned etag and adapt list success/errors identically, with not_modified mapped to empty. Rework comment explains no etag is held, so 304 is not expected. Share the review-fetch adapter within PR maintenance, but if conditional caching is later added preserve previous reviews rather than assuming 304 means none. No observed 304 incident or API saving claimed.

Both compare downcased owner/repository strings from TrackerIdentity against expected tuple. Settings additionally has a catch-all false clause; endpoint clause is narrower. Share a typed comparison primitive only while preserving caller validation/fallback policy; repository equality is not full ticket identity equality.

Both compare normalized degraded repository before module-local fetch/apply_result, with unchanged-state fallback. Related to shared subscription/repository resolution patterns, but fetch and state application remain source-specific. Prefer explicit source support policy over merging entire open-ticket and ad-hoc BuildOrder projections.

Both wrap normal results as {:ok,result}, exceptions as {:error,exception}, and all caught terms as {:error,{kind,reason}}. Candidate inside usage persistence/compaction support; preserve nested normal error returns rather than automatically flattening them. Distinct from store_unavailable or nil failure adapters.

Checkpoint/block coverage encoders serialize counts and sorted atom-name reason sets identically. Group with coverage decoder/checksum proposals in usage persistence, retaining deterministic ordering and each record format error tag. Shared serialization does not imply checkpoint and compaction block schemas merge.

Both call injected configuration_subscriber with self and treat exceptions/throws/exits as ok. Small BuildOrder process initialization pattern; the receiving process identity remains different. Retain locally unless a coherent subscription helper owns this best-effort policy, and do not represent the returned ok as proof of successful subscription.

Verified aliases resolve to the same GitHub Config/Tracker and generic Tracker facade. Both require pr_health_enabled and GitHub adapter, failing closed on exception/throw/exit. Share PR-maintenance enablement policy if these workers must remain coupled; preserve the adapter gate, not merely the config flag.

Both compare non-nil TrackerIdentity.github_key values, explicitly rejecting two nil keys as equal. Candidate for a domain identity equivalence helper shared by BuildOrder selection/adaptation. Preserve nonjoinable rejection and full repo-qualified ticket key; do not replace with raw struct equality or repository-only equality.

Verified both OpaqueIdentifier aliases resolve to Aiur.OpaqueIdentifier; heads whitelist the same agent_event/agent_alert/legacy kinds and binary names; fallbacks return nil. Candidate for a core ticket-evidence source normalizer that presentation consumes, not a core dependency on web. Preserve identifier normalization and kind allowlist.

Both datetime clauses select right only when strictly later and left on ties. Related to comment/command timestamp parsing. A narrow comment-cursor helper could share this operation, but keep nil clauses and cursor advancement policy explicit; equal timestamps may represent different record ordering elsewhere.

Both convert File.rm_rf results to ok/error reason, discarding failing path. Different ownership: membership generations versus repository sidecars. This five-line adapter alone does not justify a common destructive lifecycle abstraction; path selection and deletion authorization must remain with domain owners.

Read both callers and false clauses: skip through the first newline only when byte offset is positive, return empty if no newline, preserve contents when offset is zero. Both tail readers own descriptor cleanup. Shared bounded line-tail primitive is plausible, but alert reads collapse errors to empty whereas decision metrics propagate errors and track truncation/record limits. Preserve these consumer contracts rather than merging whole readers.

Same consumer-label fallback in credential accounting presentation and CLI: nonempty label else consumer_key else unknown when key absent. Keep explicitly nil consumer_key behavior distinct from absent-key default. Cohesive usage presentation helper candidate, not a credential identity normalization rule.

Read full clause groups: both accept positive integers or fully parsed positive strings and otherwise preserve the provider map. Share root_pid normalization within provider process metadata; preserve group IDs, remote host and process discovery as separate concerns. No proof of process liveness is supplied by a valid integer.

Both selected-root resolvers use the same RouteState, TrackerIdentity, Snapshot and SelectedRoot aliases previously inspected in complete modules. Group with shared route resolution from cluster 31dea5e1, preserving distinct analytics versus usage key adapters downstream.

Read fallback_provider_label: web splits underscore atom names into capitalized words; cost-report task merely String.capitalize on the full atom string. Known descriptor lookup agrees but unknown-provider labels differ. Consolidate descriptor lookup only or explicitly decide fallback presentation policy; whole functions are not behaviorally identical.

Both accept explicit nonempty state_dir or call Config.Paths.decision_state_dir. Candidate for a shared durable-store option resolver, preserving explicit test injection. Sharing a base directory does not establish that recent merges and webhook delivery belong in the same domain package or file.

Both PR maintenance workers use nonempty binary title else untitled. Group with their shared review/enablement support if extracted; a separate generic text package is unnecessary. Whitespace-only strings currently remain accepted.

Each @table is its own __MODULE__, so identical lookup/create bodies address distinct ETS tables. Table options and owner lifetime are part of their contracts. Do not merge snapshot publication and tracked-set state or infer race safety from this check-then-create snippet; a generic ensure_table adds little value without lifecycle ownership.

Read meaningful helpers: ad-hoc compares status/members; open tickets compares status/tickets after deleting body_excerpt. Both rebuild and broadcast on meaningful difference but intentionally ignore different fields. Preserve projection-specific equality and generation semantics; identical gate bodies are not interchangeable snapshots.

Both zip cells with widths, pad with two-space separators, and trim trailing whitespace. Candidate for local CLI tabular rendering support, preserving shortest-list zip behavior and ordinary string padding. This is not ANSI display-width-aware TUI formatting; do not substitute it for renderer Text helpers.

Both emit a Reasons sentence only for a nonempty health reason list, delegating vocabulary to reasons_text. Candidate for common web health presentation only with explicit reason rendering; full reason vocabularies are not proved equivalent by this sentence wrapper.

Both local get helpers delegate to the same Aiur.Protocol.MapAccess and both accept nonempty binary item IDs else nil. Candidate for shared protocol-field reading if ownership remains below provider transcripts. Provider event schemas and ID generation/fallback paths remain separate; do not merge entire transcript parsers.

Full deposit/read-cache parser clause groups agree: positive integer or fully consumed positive string, otherwise nil. Same behavior as earlier positive-number family modulo variable names. Group into one GitHub identifier parsing proposal, retaining repo qualification and event/cache shape classification outside it.

Both trim/lowercase strings with blank to nil. Authority has a private nonbinary fallback; CommandType gates public input before calling its binary helper. Shared decision-kind canonicalization is cohesive if public invalid-input behavior stays intact; classification and authority policy tables must remain explicit.

Read both nil and supervised start clauses plus safe_supervised_start: they try Task.Supervisor.start_child, map exits to supervisor_unavailable, then fall back to Task.start. Candidate for current-run projection task lifecycle support. Preserve caller monitoring/cancellation ownership and explicitly document unsupervised fallback; do not generalize as guaranteed supervised execution.

Quota/request-log full clause groups match the positive integer/string policy in deposit/read-cache. This also demonstrates exact hashes undercount semantic duplicates because names of invalid variables differ. Deduplicate these sites with the same numeric family rather than count a separate package opportunity.

Both combine known and guessed branches into the same entry shape including known_branch boolean. Helpers were inspected in earlier clusters and preserve identical ordering/precedence. Consolidate this complete poll branch-selection subroutine rather than separately extracting each tiny helper.

Both runtimes derive the selected TrackerIdentity GitHub key or nil through RouteState. Group with BuildOrder route-resolution support; preserve nonjoinable nil and keep analytics/usage cache key types and access gates independent.

Body references provider-local section_value and different defaults: aiur-claude versus codex app-server. Therefore it does not represent the same command configuration. Both validate nonempty before trimming, so whitespace-only input becomes empty; any normalization change needs its own contract decision. Shared mechanics must not conflate provider sections or defaults.

Read all clauses: both accept DateTime directly or parsed ISO string and return error otherwise. Candidate for telemetry-owned timestamp validation shared by writer/dataset. Preserve actual DateTime values and parsing errors; not equivalent to nil-returning UI timestamp helpers.

Both full enum groups accept allowed atoms or strings matching allowed atom names, else caller-provided error. Candidate for usage schema validation support. Preserve explicit allowlists, case sensitivity and absence of dynamic atom creation; each price/relationship schema still owns its allowed values.

Both project review_decision and head_committed_at keys; webhook helper is map-guarded. Share the event context shape within GitHub review events, preserving nil when upstream lacks enrichment. Extraction does not make missing REST/webhook review data available or activate an otherwise inert gate.

Quota and request log derive ticket:<digits> from issues/pulls URL paths with the same regex. Candidate for shared request attribution policy with number validators; preserve path-only attribution, which does not authenticate host, repository or user identity. Do not claim this is a full ticket identity parser.

Same apply-result notification skeleton calls source-local do_apply_result and meaningful; the earlier review established different member/ticket shapes and excerpt exclusion. Group with source change gating, retaining projection-specific equality and recovery semantics.

Both prefer an existing atom key even when its value is nil/false, falling back to string key only when absent. Existing Protocol.MapAccess.get uses || and therefore differs. Any shared accessor must name presence-versus-truthiness semantics; do not replace these with get merely because both support atom/string keys. Lifecycle additionally guards atom key.

Verified both Bounded and Diagnostic aliases resolve to the same BuildOrder modules. Both adapt github_url into value plus optional invalid_url diagnostic. Group with identity-bound URL adapter in the same domain; do not confuse generic URL validation with matching a specific issue identity.

MessageHandler timestamp_for duplicates existing Protocol.MapAccess.message_timestamp exactly, including atom/string || precedence and utc_now fallback for anything except DateTime. Reuse that existing protocol owner if dependency direction permits. Preserve the difference between receive-time fallback and parsing persisted ISO timestamps; no claim that fallback proves source freshness.

Same TrackerIdentity.github_key-to-ok/error helper previously reviewed with normalize_tickets. Group those helpers into one usage scoping proposal; do not count this as a separate extraction or saving.

Both use the same OpaqueIdentifier normalizer and omit rejected values without deleting an existing map key. Group with ticket-evidence normalization below web presentation. Preserve existing-map behavior when input is invalid; replacing it with Map.put nil would differ.

TrackerHealth privately repeats public Connectivity.streak_count behavior: valid positive stored count or default one. Candidate to reuse existing connectivity ownership; preserve guards/caller typing and the policy that absent count is one rather than zero. This is not an elapsed-time or outage-duration measurement.

Same ISO-string-to-DateTime-or-nil clause under catalog datetime and review freshness parse. Related to earlier comment/UI timestamp cluster with renamed variables; compare full input policies before sharing. No generic date package justified by this one clause alone.

Actual @table_min_width differs: GitHub cost 96 columns, units 120. Share terminal-width detection only with caller-owned minimum or retain the small wrappers. Identical bodies do not authorize a common threshold; nonterminal/narrow fallback to records must stay explicit.

Matching named/public ETS creation skeleton references different module-local @table values for active turns and tokens. Preserve lifecycle, ownership, access and cleanup boundaries; do not merge registries or infer concurrent creation safety from identical code.

Both parse the first ticket.<non-dot>. segment with identical regex and return nil otherwise. Candidate for a shared event-topic contract below alert/wake projections. Preserve permissive identifier syntax; this does not prove a topic is trusted or bound to a subscriber.

Read full clause groups: both accept nonnegative integer or fully parsed string, otherwise nil. Cohesive usage drill-input helper for both web runtimes, preserving zero as valid and keeping financial access checks separate.

Both invoke injected now_fun and accept only DateTime, returning nil for other normal results. Small source-local contract; exceptions still propagate. Group only with coherent source support, not a global clock abstraction that silently changes failure handling.

Threshold/retention attributes differ: agent process log 4,194,304 bytes and eight generations; request log 1,048,576 bytes and two generations. Shared rotation mechanism is plausible with explicit parameters, preserving strict greater-than threshold and distinct retention policy. No storage or cost saving measured.

GitHub Issues and Linear client match ISO parsing body but call boundaries/public visibility differ. Candidate for tracker record conversion only after full clause/caller policy review; neither this body nor matching timestamp shape makes tracker adapters equivalent. Group with timestamp near-duplicate family.

Both map DateTime.from_iso8601 errors to nil; takeover helper is binary-guarded while metrics helper is internally called. Preserve input validation and caller-specific unavailable semantics. Related to other ISO parsing clauses, not an independent package opportunity.

Both stop a live pid normally with 1,000 ms timeout, swallowing exits. Candidate for display-tailer lifecycle ownership across runner/provider boundary. Preserve type guards at callers and distinguish graceful stop from unconditional kill; a successful return can include swallowed timeout/exit.

Both previously inspected scope modules extract Snapshot.authority_epoch or unknown through the same RouteState helper. Group with shared selected-root resolution; preserve authority epoch versus snapshot generation because downstream cache identity depends on the distinction.

Both use the same GraphQLCost.reported nonnegative cost or assumed one. Read neighboring clauses: both special-case 304 to zero, but request-log API wraps success/error and tags failed requests assumed while quota takes separate status/response arguments. Share cost classification through an explicit normalized response contract; preserve reported/assumed provenance and error handling.

Read both complete workpad predicates and body accessors: same string/atom body fallback, trim-leading and Agent Workpad prefix check, false for nonmaps. Candidate to reuse existing Events.CommentFilter.agent_workpad? from comment context if boundary permits. It checks a prefix, not author trust; preserve separate trusted-comment checks.

Both parse ISO strings to ok timestamp/error; group with BuildOrder evidence/date normalization only after preserving other input clauses. Different from nil-returning display helpers; do not erase success/error shape when consolidating timestamp families.

Both delegate Task.Supervisor.terminate_child and swallow exit/error catches, not arbitrary throws. Cohesive BuildOrder task-lifecycle helper candidate, preserving caller monitors/timers and supervised-task ownership. Return ok after a caught failure is not proof the child was stopped.

Read complete optional timestamp clauses: Claude bounds seconds to 253402300799 and accepts floats via rounded milliseconds; Codex accepts nonnegative integers and nil only. Shared integer conversion may be useful, but do not merge whole adapters or silently admit fractional Codex values. Preserve provider-specific format validation.
Same head/ref lookup already inspected with known_branch. Group into the complete CI/comment branch selection subroutine, retaining malformed/non-map fallback; no separate extraction count.

Both normalize_atom helpers accept allowed atoms or exact matching atom-name strings, otherwise nil. Group with earlier price/relationship enum validation, keeping caller-owned allowlists/error values and avoiding atom creation. This is one validation family, not multiple independent package proposals.

Both adapters use the same Bounded.github_issue_url_for and Diagnostic modules, preserving identity-bound URL checking and invalid_url diagnostic. Share alongside generic URL adaptation only with explicit distinction between generic and issue-bound checks.
